author: Blyth, 1849
summary: 국내에서는 지금까지 기록이 10건 미만인 길잃은새이다. 유럽 동북부에서 시베리아 남부와 중앙아시아에 걸쳐 번식하고, 인도·스리랑카 등 남아시아에서 겨울을 난다. 다른 개개비 무리와 달리 갈대밭보다 물가 덤불, 숲 가장자리, 정원 같은 곳에서 많이 지낸다.

points.en: short whitish supercilium, mainly in front of the eye
plain closed wing with little contrast

art.subject: Blyth's Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus dumetorum), adult (sexes alike) in autumn: upperparts plain olive-brown to greyish-brown, the rump at most faintly warmer and never contrastingly rufous; a short whitish supercilium, most obvious in front of the eye and fading just behind it; dark lores; throat white; underparts off-white with a faint buffish-grey wash on the breast sides and flanks; wings plain, the tertials uniform with little contrast; tail plain brown; bill dark with a pale pinkish lower mandible; dark eye; greyish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched in a leafy shrub, side view
art.scene: shrubby woodland edge on a Korean offshore island during autumn migration in September, soft light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult (sexes alike) in autumn, side view perched in a leafy shrub: slim, round-headed reed warbler, short whitish supercilium mainly in front of the eye, dusky line through the eye, long slender bill, plain olive-brown upperparts, plain closed wing with little contrast, plain off-white underparts, plain brown rounded tail

adult, head and upper body in profile: short whitish supercilium from the bill base to the eye, barely reaching behind it, dusky eye-stripe, dark eye, long slender bill, white throat, plain olive-brown crown and nape
art.build: A small, plain reed warbler, about sparrow length but slimmer, much smaller than an Oriental Reed Warbler; round-headed with a fairly steep forehead. Bill fairly long and thin, slightly shorter than the head. Legs medium, greyish. Wings short and rounded: the primary projection is short, clearly shorter than the tertials. Tail medium, rounded, plain, without white. Often found in bushes and woodland edges rather than reeds.
avoid: Do not paint a long supercilium running well behind the eye or a dark line above it (Black-browed Reed or Paddyfield Warbler).
Do not paint a bright rufous rump contrasting with the back, or rich tawny upperparts; the upperparts are plain olive-brown, at most faintly warmer on the rump.
Do not paint streaks on the back or breast.
Do not make it large and heavy-billed like Oriental Reed Warbler.
